newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Feb motor vehicle output down 7 pct - VDA.
newsitem.headline: German Feb motor vehicle output down 7 pct - VDA.

text.p: German motor vehicle production fell seven percent year-on-year in February and car production also fell seven percent due in part to the impact of a Spanish truckers strike which blocked deliveries of car components, the VDA Automobile Industry Association said. It provided the following figures.
Feb 97 pct chg yr/yr Feb 97 pct chg

NOTE - The VDA also said that domestic new orders for cars rose 15 percent in February from February 1997 but added that the increase was explained by the "extremely low" order volume in the year-earlier month. On a seasonally adjusted basis domestic demand remained weak, the association said.

Foreign new car orders rose five percent. Domestic orders for trucks were down three percent year-on-year while foreign orders for trucks rose five percent, due mainly to a 43 percent surge in orders for heavy trucks.
New car registrations in February fell three percent year-on-year to an estimated 258,000 units but on a seasonally-adjusted basis they rose slightly from January 1997, the VDA said.
